title: Pegasus: egress-resolver affinity rebind after peering topology reshuffle causing cross-tenant name resolution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Two paying Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant hostname mappings (private hostnames resolving to shared egress IPs) immediately following a scheduled peering topology reshuffle and a concurrent autoscaler event. Issue surfaced as customer escalations (support tickets #C-12981, #C-12989) and impacted production traffic for a 6-22 minute window in each incident. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, fix, rollout, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two dedicated tenants with VPC peering to a shared egress region.
2) Trigger a peering topology change (resync/reparent) while performing a rapid scale-down of GPU node pool that causes egress-proxy pods to move.
3) Run repeated outbound name resolutions for tenant-private hostnames and observe intermittent responses resolving to the other tenant's egress IPs.
4) Capture conntrack state, SNAT allocations, and resolver affinity logs on egress nodes during the window.
Observed: resolver affinity and SNAT bindings were occasionally mis-associated for short windows after node reassignment/reparenting.
observations: Issue coincided with peering topology change + autoscaler activity (race condition window).
Cross-tenant name resolution correlated with resolver affinity loss: requests answered by an egress-resolver instance that had stale tenant binding metadata.
Conntrack entries showed ephemeral SNAT ports reused in combinations that permitted replies to be routed back to the wrong tenant path during the convergence window.
Affected requests were TCP/HTTPS and DNS-over-UDP; TTLs and cache invalidation behavior amplified the window for some customers.
No evidence of data exfiltration; traffic reached the intended endpoint but DNS answered with an IP from the wrong tenant's egress pool in intermittent bursts.
root_cause: Control-plane recomputation of tenant->egress-resolver bindings during peering reparenting was non-atomic and raced with the node-level egress-proxy reassignment. The egress-proxy used ephemeral in-memory resolver affinity coupled with shared SNAT port pools. During the race, a newly reassigned proxy accepted flows before the control-plane binding update was durably persisted, leading to transient mappings where a tenant's requests were forwarded to a proxy still answering with another tenant's resolver context. Additionally, shared SNAT port ranges allowed reply multiplexing in rare timing windows.
resolution: Code fix: make tenant->resolver binding update atomic in the control plane - introduce a lease-based two-phase update so egress-proxies only accept tenant traffic after durable assignment. Runtime change: allocate per-tenant SNAT port subranges by default for Dedicated pools and fall back to shared ranges only when explicitly configured. Added reconciliation loop that backfills durable resolver bindings on node startup. Configuration change: enable 'tenant_pinned_snat' for affected regions. Infrastructure migration: run a one-time backfill to persist resolver bindings for currently running proxies.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs and run unit + integration suites in CI.
2) Canary deploy to 'dedicated-us-west-2a' (5% tenants) with tenant_pinned_snat enabled and enhanced audit logging for resolver-binding events.
3) Monitor canary for 48 hours; required metrics: cross_tenant_dns_rate < 0.01% of total queries, resolver_binding_failures == 0, snat_port_exhaustion == 0.
4) Gradual rollout across dedicated regions over 7 days with automatic rollback if cross_tenant_dns_rate > threshold or error spikes occur.
5) Once stable, backfill bindings for all active proxies and toggle tenant_pinned_snat as default for Dedicated tier.
Rollback plan: revert config and redeploy previous egress-proxy image; reopen preserved state in control plane to previous consistent binding state.
monitoring_and_alerts: New metrics added: resolver_binding_age, resolver_binding_mismatch_count, tenant_snat_port_overlap_count.
Dashboards: Dedicated -> Egress -> Pegasus Canary (link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/pegasus)
Alerts: P0 alert if resolver_binding_mismatch_count > 5 in 1m for production regions; PagerDuty escalation to oncall-networking.
Audit logs: enable verbose tenant->resolver binding logs for 72 hours post-rollout.
qa_test_plan: Integration: simulate peering reparent + rapid egress-proxy relocation; assert no cross-tenant DNS answers in 10k queries.
Chaos: pod termination and node drain during controlled peering resync; validate atomic binding acquisition and no DNS mismatch.
Load: synthetic workload at 2x normal traffic to ensure SNAT per-tenant pools prevent port reuse degradation.
Backward compatibility: ensure Hosted and Shared tiers unaffected; validate Dedicated-only behavior under config flag.
postmortem_actions: Documented incident timeline and root cause in Confluence (PEG-2026-01-28).
Notify affected customers with detailed timeline and mitigation steps; customer success to offer dedicated RCA calls.
Create follow-up tickets to: audit other control-plane non-atomic updates (ENG-331500), add long-term SNAT allocation manager (ENG-332000), and update runbooks for peering maintenance windows.
Schedule a security review for the change (security_review_required=true) and include SRE for verification.
